question: What primary role does the peripheral nervous system perform in the human body?

options.A: Generates primary hormones to control metabolic rate
options.B: Produces cerebrospinal fluid to cushion brain tissue
options.C: Processes complex abstract thoughts and long-term memory
options.D: Connects the central nervous system to body organs and limbs

explanation: The PNS serves as the vital link carrying signals between the central nervous system and peripheral tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h1)

question: A patient loses sensation in their fingers after a wrist injury. Which anatomical division is primarily affected?
explanation: Nerves traveling through the limbs to the fingers belong to the peripheral nervous system. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h1)

question: Name the innermost connective tissue layer that directly surrounds an individual nerve fiber.
explanation: The endoneurium is the delicate layer wrapping each individual nerve fiber within a fascicle. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the tough epineurium layer surrounding a peripheral nerve?

options.A: Generates electrical impulses to speed up signal transmission along axons
options.B: Produces myelin to insulate nerve fibers from surrounding tissue fluid
options.C: Provides structural strength and mechanical protection against physical damage
options.D: Releases neurotransmitters directly across the synaptic cleft during contraction

explanation: The outer epineurium acts as a tough protective casing shielding inner nerve fascicles from stretch and trauma. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h2)

question: How many pairs of cranial nerves emerge directly from the brain?
explanation: The human body has 12 distinct pairs of cranial nerves controlling head, neck, and organ functions. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h3)

question: A patient cannot move their left eye outward toward the ear. Which cranial nerve is likely impaired?
explanation: The abducens nerve controls the lateral rectus muscle responsible for turning the eye outward. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the total number of spinal nerve pairs in the human body?
explanation: There are 31 paired spinal nerves distributed across the cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral, and coccygeal regions. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why do spinal nerves in the limbs form nerve plexuses instead of running straight to muscles?

options.A: The thoracic vertebrae lack enough space to let individual nerve branches pass through
options.B: Nerve plexuses exclusively carry autonomic signals while spinal nerves carry somatic signals
options.C: Interweaving fibers allow multiple spinal segments to supply single limb muscles for protection
options.D: Plexuses completely bypass the spinal cord to speed up reflex reactions

explanation: Plexuses blend fibers from different levels so that injury to a single spinal segment does not completely paralyze a limb. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which sensory receptor type is responsible for detecting painful or damaging stimuli?
explanation: Nociceptors are specialized nerve endings that signal potential or actual tissue damage experienced as pain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h5)

question: A patient feels a gentle breeze on their skin. Which peripheral receptor type detects this sensation?
explanation: Mechanoreceptors detect mechanical forces like touch, pressure, vibration, and light skin movement. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary target tissue of the somatic nervous system?
explanation: The somatic system specifically controls voluntary actions involving skeletal muscles. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h6)

question: How many motor neurons typically link the central nervous system to skeletal muscle in a somatic pathway?

options.B: Two neurons connected by an autonomic ganglion
options.C: A chain of three interconnected sensory neurons
options.D: Multiple short interneurons crossing the spinal cord

explanation: Somatic motor pathways feature one long neuron traveling directly from the spinal cord to the target muscle. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which autonomic division is primarily responsible for the 'fight-or-flight' response during stress?
explanation: The sympathetic nervous system prepares the body for physical action or emergency responses. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h7)

question: What structural feature distinguishes autonomic motor pathways from somatic motor pathways?

options.A: Autonomic pathways do not utilize chemical neurotransmitters
options.B: Autonomic pathways use a two-neuron chain with a ganglion
options.C: Autonomic pathways rely exclusively on a single myelinated axon
options.D: Autonomic pathways only connect to skeletal muscle fibers

explanation: Autonomic pathways require a preganglionic and postganglionic neuron sequence before reaching target organs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of a reflex arc in the human body?

options.A: To produce rapid, involuntary protective responses without conscious thought
options.B: To regulate long-term hormonal balance throughout the endocrine system
options.C: To consciously coordinate precise multi-step skeletal muscle movements
options.D: To send conscious sensory signals to the brain for complex analysis

explanation: Reflex arcs allow instant reactions to dangerous stimuli without waiting for brain processing. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h8)

question: Which component of a reflex arc directly carries the nerve impulse away from the spinal cord to an effector?
explanation: Motor (efferent) neurons transmit signals out of the central nervous system to muscles or glands. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h8)

question: Which systemic chronic condition is a leading cause of peripheral neuropathy in clinical practice?
explanation: Chronically elevated blood sugar levels damage peripheral nerve fibers over time, causing diabetic neuropathy. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h9)

question: Why must nurses instruct patients with peripheral neuropathy to perform daily visual foot inspections?

options.A: Inspectors can apply topical neurotransmitters to restore local reflexes
options.B: Daily washing is the only way to reverse nerve cell degeneration
options.C: Numbness prevents them from feeling injuries or cuts on their feet
options.D: Visual checks stimulate the regeneration of damaged myelin sheaths

explanation: Loss of protective sensation means patients will not notice blisters, cuts, or sores without looking. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h9)
